quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "Morning glory flowers unfurling their petals as the sun rises". What time of day is it?
quests.question: Morning glory flowers unfurling their petals as the sun rises
quests.hint: Think about the name of this flower — it's a clue all by itself!
quests.explanation: Yes! Morning glory flowers open as the sun rises, right at the start of the day.
quests.funFact: Morning glory flowers actually close back up again later in the afternoon!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "Moonflowers slowly unfurling their pale white petals after sunset". What time of day is it?
quests.question: Moonflowers slowly unfurling their pale white petals after sunset
quests.hint: Think about what this flower's petals do once daylight fades.
quests.explanation: Yes! Moonflowers open after sunset, once night has begun.
quests.funFact: Moonflowers are pollinated by moths, which is why they bloom at night instead of during the day!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A sunflower field slowly turning to track the sun's path"?
quests.question: A sunflower field slowly turning to track the sun's path
quests.hint: Think about when the sun's path can actually be tracked across the sky.
quests.explanation: Yes! Sunflowers track the sun's path as it moves across the daytime sky.
quests.funFact: Young sunflowers turn from east to west, following the sun throughout the day!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "An evening primrose opening its blossoms as the light fades"?
quests.question: An evening primrose opening its blossoms as the light fades
quests.hint: Think about the name of this flower — it hints at when it blooms.
quests.explanation: Yes! Evening primrose opens its blossoms once daylight fades, at night.
quests.funFact: This flower's blossoms can open in just a few minutes, almost fast enough to watch!

quests.instruction: "Bees and butterflies visiting blossoms that have opened wide" — when does this happen?
quests.question: Bees and butterflies visiting blossoms that have opened wide
quests.hint: Think about when bees and butterflies are usually out and about.
quests.explanation: Yes! Bees and butterflies are typically active and visiting flowers during the day.
quests.funFact: Bees can actually see colors that are invisible to the human eye!

quests.instruction: "A rare cactus flower blooming for just a few dark hours" — when does this happen?
quests.question: A rare cactus flower blooming for just a few dark hours
quests.hint: Think about the words 'dark hours' — when do those happen?
quests.explanation: Yes! This rare flower opens only during the dark hours of night.
quests.funFact: Some night-blooming cactus flowers open for only one single night each year!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A spider's dew-covered web sparkling in the early sunlight". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.question: A spider's dew-covered web sparkling in the early sunlight
quests.hint: Think about the word 'sunlight' — it's a strong clue all by itself.
quests.explanation: Yes! Sunlight tells you it's daytime, even though the dew formed earlier.
quests.funFact: Spider webs are made of silk that's actually stronger than steel of the same thickness!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A silkworm moth fluttering quietly around a porch lamp"?
quests.question: A silkworm moth fluttering quietly around a porch lamp
quests.hint: Think about when a porch lamp would actually be glowing and switched on.
quests.explanation: Yes! A glowing porch lamp means it's dark outside, so it's nighttime.
quests.funFact: Silkworm moths have been carefully raised by people for thousands of years to make silk thread!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Tadpoles wriggling near the sunny surface of a shallow pond"?
quests.question: Tadpoles wriggling near the sunny surface of a shallow pond
quests.hint: Think about the word 'sunny' — it's telling you something about the light.
quests.explanation: Yes! A sunny pond surface tells you it's daytime.
quests.funFact: Tadpoles slowly grow legs and lungs as they transform into frogs!

quests.instruction: "Cool dew slowly forming on blades of grass as the air cools after dark" — when does this happen?
quests.question: Cool dew slowly forming on blades of grass as the air cools after dark
quests.hint: Think about when the air outside cools down enough for dew to form.
quests.explanation: Yes! Dew forms overnight, as the air cools once the sun goes down.
quests.funFact: Dew forms when warm, moist air touches a cool surface, like grass at night!

quests.instruction: "A caterpillar munching steadily on a sunlit leaf" — when does this happen?
quests.question: A caterpillar munching steadily on a sunlit leaf
quests.hint: Think about the word 'sunlit' — it's a clue about the light outside.
quests.explanation: Yes! A sunlit leaf tells you it's daytime.
quests.funFact: A caterpillar can eat many times its own body weight in leaves before becoming a butterfly!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "A pond's surface rippling as nocturnal fish rise to feed". What time of day is it?
quests.question: A pond's surface rippling as nocturnal fish rise to feed
quests.hint: Think about when these fish usually feel safest to come out and feed.
quests.explanation: Yes! Nocturnal fish are most active and feeding at night.
quests.funFact: Some fish have extra-sensitive eyes that help them hunt well in low light!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "Migrating geese flying in a V-shape across a clear blue sky". What time of day is it?
quests.question: Migrating geese flying in a V-shape across a clear blue sky
quests.hint: Think about the words 'clear blue sky' — when do we see a sky like that?
quests.explanation: Yes! A clear blue sky tells you it's daytime.
quests.funFact: Geese fly in a V-shape to help save energy by riding the wind off each other's wings!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Bats swooping low over a still pond to catch insects in the dark"?
quests.question: Bats swooping low over a still pond to catch insects in the dark
quests.hint: Think about the word 'dark' — it's a clue about the time.
quests.explanation: Yes! Bats hunt for insects in the dark, at night.
quests.funFact: A single bat can eat thousands of insects in just one night!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A field of wheat swaying golden under the midday sun"?
quests.question: A field of wheat swaying golden under the midday sun
quests.hint: Think about when the sun sits at its very highest point.
quests.explanation: Yes! Midday is the middle of the daytime.
quests.funFact: A single wheat field can produce enough grain to bake thousands of loaves of bread!

quests.instruction: "Streetlights glowing brightly against a completely black sky" — when does this happen?
quests.question: Streetlights glowing brightly against a completely black sky
quests.hint: Think about the words 'completely black sky' — when do we see a sky like that?
quests.explanation: Yes! A completely black sky is a clear sign of nighttime.
quests.funFact: Streetlights help drivers and walkers stay safe once it's dark outside!

quests.instruction: "A bright, cloudless sky stretching from one horizon to the other" — when does this happen?
quests.question: A bright, cloudless sky stretching from one horizon to the other
quests.hint: Think about the word 'bright' — when is the sky usually this bright?
quests.explanation: Yes! A bright sky like this is a clear sign of daytime.
quests.funFact: On a perfectly clear day, you can sometimes see for over 60 miles!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "An orchestra's final encore before the concert hall empties into a dark parking lot"?
quests.question: An orchestra's final encore before the concert hall empties into a dark parking lot
quests.hint: Think about the word 'dark' — it's a clue about the parking lot outside.
quests.explanation: Yes! A dark parking lot tells you the concert ended at night.
quests.funFact: An encore happens when an excited audience claps and cheers for the performers to play just a little more!

quests.instruction: "Sunlight filling the classroom, even though every lamp inside is switched off" — when does this happen?
quests.question: Sunlight filling the classroom, even though every lamp inside is switched off
quests.hint: Think about what's lighting up the room if the lamps are all off.
quests.explanation: Yes! If sunlight alone fills the room, it must be daytime outside.
quests.funFact: Many classrooms are designed with big windows to let in plenty of natural light!

quests.instruction: "A shopping mall long closed, its halls dim and completely empty" — when does this happen?
quests.question: A shopping mall long closed, its halls dim and completely empty
quests.hint: Think about when a busy shopping mall would finally be closed and empty.
quests.explanation: Yes! A mall this quiet and closed suggests it's very late at night.
quests.funFact: Many stores use security cameras and alarms to help keep things safe overnight!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "A busy shopping mall filled with daylight streaming through skylights". What time of day is it?
quests.question: A busy shopping mall filled with daylight streaming through skylights
quests.hint: Think about the word 'daylight' — it's a clue all by itself.
quests.explanation: Yes! Daylight streaming through skylights tells you it's daytime.
quests.funFact: Skylights help stores save energy by using natural sunlight instead of electric lights!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A farmer double-checking that the barn doors are shut before heading inside to sleep"?
quests.question: A farmer double-checking that the barn doors are shut before heading inside to sleep
quests.hint: Think about what 'before heading inside to sleep' tells you about the time.
quests.explanation: Yes! Heading inside to sleep tells you it's already nighttime.
quests.funFact: Farmers check on their animals and barns to make sure everyone stays safe overnight!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "An orchestra rehearsing on a sunlit stage before the evening show"?
quests.question: An orchestra rehearsing on a sunlit stage before the evening show
quests.hint: Think about the word 'sunlit' and the word 'before' — has evening happened yet?
quests.explanation: Yes! A sunlit stage before the evening show tells you it's still daytime.
quests.funFact: Orchestras often rehearse for many hours to prepare for just one evening performance!

quests.instruction: "A backyard full of twinkling stars, with not a single cloud in sight" — when does this happen?
quests.question: A backyard full of twinkling stars, with not a single cloud in sight
quests.hint: Think about when twinkling stars are visible in the sky.
quests.explanation: Yes! Twinkling stars are a clear sign of nighttime.
quests.funFact: Stars twinkle because their light passes through moving layers of our atmosphere!

quests.instruction: "A farmer checking on crops beneath a wide, sunny sky" — when does this happen?
quests.question: A farmer checking on crops beneath a wide, sunny sky
quests.hint: Think about when farmers usually walk their fields to check on crops.
quests.explanation: Yes! A sunny sky tells you it's daytime.
quests.funFact: Farmers check their crops often to watch for the very best time to harvest!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A pair of glowing eyes peeking out from a hollow log in the moonlight"?
quests.question: A pair of glowing eyes peeking out from a hollow log in the moonlight
quests.hint: Think about the word 'moonlight' — when does the moon actually shine?
quests.explanation: Yes! Moonlight only shines at night, so this hollow log is being seen after dark.
quests.funFact: Many small animals have eyes that seem to glow because of a special layer that helps them see in the dark!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A scientist carefully labeling animal bones at a sunny desk in the lab". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.question: A scientist carefully labeling animal bones at a sunny desk in the lab
quests.hint: Think about the word "sunny" — it is a clue about the light in the room.
quests.explanation: Yes! A sunny desk tells you it is daytime, even though the scientist might be studying animals that are active at night.
quests.funFact: Scientists who study animals often work during the day, even when their research is about nighttime creatures!

quests.instruction: "A violin case being packed up after the very last song of a candlelit concert" — when does this happen?
quests.question: A violin case being packed up after the very last song of a candlelit concert
quests.hint: Think about the word 'candlelit' — when would candles be needed for light?
quests.explanation: Yes! A candlelit concert happens once it's dark outside, at night.
quests.funFact: Candlelit concerts are a cozy, old-fashioned way to enjoy music by soft, warm light!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A planetarium show beginning just as the theater lights dim completely". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.question: A planetarium show beginning just as the theater lights dim completely
quests.hint: Think about whether a planetarium show can be held even if it's actually still light outside.
quests.explanation: Yes! Planetarium shows create their own dark, starry sky indoors, so they can happen even during the day outside.
quests.funFact: A planetarium uses a special projector to show thousands of stars on a domed ceiling!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "A cool breeze rustling the curtains while the whole street sleeps in darkness". What time of day is it?
quests.question: A cool breeze rustling the curtains while the whole street sleeps in darkness
quests.hint: Think about what 'the whole street sleeps in darkness' is telling you.
quests.explanation: Yes! A sleeping, dark street is a clear sign that it's nighttime.
quests.funFact: A cool nighttime breeze can help make a bedroom feel just right for sleeping!
